Bagh, Delhi, in respect of commission of offence of causing simple hurt, to the victim Baljeet Singh and grievous hurt sustained by the victim Shyam Singh/petitioner herein, by rash and negligent driving of a motor vehicle, on a public road, punishable U/s 279/337/338 of Indian Penal Code,
1860 (hereinafter referred to as IPC).

Subsequently, a final report under Section 173 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (herein afterwards referred as Cr.P.C), was filed against respondent no. 1 namely Gopal Kishan, for the alleged commission of offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
2.

The brief facts of the case as discernible from the DAR and documents of the injured are that on 11.02.2018, at about 7:45 p.m., when both the injured namely Baljeet Singh and Shyam Singh were going towards Shakur Basti Railway Station and reached near Haryana Maitri Bhawan, at road no.
44, Rani Bagh, Delhi, on their Hero Honda motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-3SBN-1849,
(hereinafter referred as victim's vehicle), on which, injured Baljeet Singh was sitting as a pillion rider, they were hit from behind, by one Ritz Car bearing registration no. DL-8CW-6912 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle), which was being driven at a very high speed, rashly, negligently,
dangerously, in a zig-zag manner and without blowing horn, by its driver Gopal Kishan (hereinafter referred as the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no.1/R1), due to which, they both fell down on the metallic road.
It is further alleged that the petitioner namely Shyam Singh sustained grievous injuries on spine, which was later diagnosed fracture and his son in law namely Baljeet Singh suffered simple injuries.

It is further pleaded that the PCR van took both the injured to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, where they received medical treatment but, in the MLC of the petitioner, the name, father's name and address were wrongly mentioned, which was subsequently corrected by the hospital staff in the subsequent treatment papers.
3. R1 failed to contest the case of the petitioner, by filing any written statement hence, his defence was struck off vide order dated 15.02.2019.

4. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., the insurer of the offending vehicle (hereinafter referred as the respondent no.2/R2), had filed the written statement/legal offer, raising the contention, that at the time of accident, the petitioner was neither having any driving license nor the victim's vehicle was insured therefore, R2 has filed the legal offer of Rs. 32,224/-, by deducting 50% on account of contributory negligence, on the part of the petitioner but, R2 admitted existence of insurance policy no. 215500/31/20184901 for the period 19.12.2017 to 18.12.2018, qua the offending vehicle.
5.

From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Learned Predecessor Court, vide order dated 15.02.2019:-
(1)

Whether on 11.02.2018, at about 7:45 p.m., at Rishi Nagar, Road no. 43, Opposite Shakur Basti Railway Station, Delhi, one car bearing registration no.
DL-3SBN-1849, which was being driving rashly and negligently by Gopal Kishan, hit the motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-8CW-6912 and caused injuries to Shyam Singh ?

OPP. 
(2)Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP (3)
Relief.

4 6.
After framing of issues, opportunities were given to all the parties to prove their respective averments, by leading evidence in support of the same.
In support of his case, the petitioner got examined three witnesses.
7. The petitioner/injured Shyam Singh got himself examined as PW1.
He led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A and has placed reliance upon the copy of DAR Ex. PW1/1 and his medical bills Ex. PW1/2.
His deposition qua the accident in question is reiteration of the contents of FIR as well as DAR.
He further deposed that R1 was arrested in FIR No. 40/18 U/s 279/338 IPC, PS Rani Bagh and the said case is pending trial before Ld. MM.
He further deposed that he has spent more than 2 Lakh rupees on his treatment.
He further deposed that he was doing the work of shuttering (saria bandhne ka kaam) and was earning about 25,000/- per month.
He deposed that since in the accident, he has suffered 12% permanent disability, due to which, he was not able to do his job and unable to carry weight therefore, his disability be taken as 100%.
He further deposed that after the accident, he remained bed ridden for 6 months.

8. PW1 was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for R2, wherein he admitted that on the date of accident,
he was not having valid driving license, to drive the motorcycle and that his vehicle was not insured.
He further deposed that he was the registered owner of the motorcycle.
He deposed that he was going to meet his mother at Wazirpur from Sultanpuri but, he denied the suggestion that he was drunk on the date of accident.
He also denied the suggestion that neither he nor Baljeet Singh were wearing helmet, at the time of accident.

He deposed that he was driving the motorcycle on the left side of the road and that the offending vehicle came from backside and after the accident, the offending car stopped and the driver of the offending car as well as police shifted him to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital.
He further admitted that his entire treatment has taken place at Government hospital but, he deposed that he took the medicines from market.
He denied the suggestion that he has not spent Rs. 2 lakhs on medical treatment.
He admitted that he has not placed on record, any document to prove his income of Rs. 25,000/- per month.
He deposed that at present, he is not doing his previous work of shuttering, as he is not able to lift heavy weight.
He further deposed that he is not doing any work as on date.
He further deposed that he is married, having four children and monthly expenditure of his family is about 20/25,000/- per month.
He deposed that his three sons are major and earning separately.
He denied the suggestion that the accident occurred due to his negligence or that there is no negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle.

9. PW2/Dr. Manish Kumar, S.R. Orthopedic, Dr. BSA Hospital, was a summoned witness, who deposed that he has appeared on behalf of Dr. Gurvinder Singh, Assistant Professor, Department of Orthopedics, Dr. BSA Hospital.

He exhibited the disability certificate no. 1547, dated 11.05.2018,
along with the assessment proforma as Ex. PW2/A, issued by the Doctors of Disability Board,
consisting of Dr. Gurvinder Singh, qua the patient Shyam Singh, by identifying the signatures of Dr.
Gurvinder Singh, stating that he has worked under him.

He deposed that as per the disability certificate, the patient suffered permanent disability to the tune of 12 %, in relation to spine, with diagnosis of post traumatic wedge compression, with fracture of D12 vertebral body.
He deposed that the patient would feel pain by walking on slope, he cannot climb stairs without support and cannot squat properly.
He further deposed that the patient would feel moderate difficulty in taking turns.

5 10.

During the course of examination of PW2, court question was put to PW2, as to whether the patient could continue his work of shuttering with the said permanent disability, to which, PW2 deposed that as the patient has suffered permanent disability in relation to spine and cannot climb stairs without support hence, the patient would feel considerable difficulty in doing the said work.
11. PW2 was also cross examined by Ld. Counsel for R2, wherein PW2 deposed that he was not the treating doctor of the patient and has deposed only as per record.
PW2 deposed that the Board has physically examined the patient and checked his X- Ray, before issuing the report.
He denied the suggestion that the permanent disability as assessed, was at a higher side, to help the patient and not as per rules and regulations.
He denied the suggestion that the patient would not feel difficulty in doing his work with permanent disability.
12. The petitioner has further examined Sh. Ved Singh as PW3.

He has tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW3/A, wherein he deposed that he is a friend and co-worker with the petitioner and he used to do the same work of shuttering, which the petitioner was doing.
He deposed that he has worked with the petitioner at many sites.
He further deposed that on 11.02.2018, the petitioner has met with an accident and suffered various injuries and since then, he has stopped the work of shuttering, as he has suffered spine injuries.
He further deposed that in the work of shuttering, a person has to use lot of physical power and has to carry lot of weight.
He further deposed that a person doing the work of shuttering can easily earn Rs. 25,000/- per month.
13. PW3 was also cross examined by Ld. Counsel for R2, wherein he deposed that he has no document, to prove that he was doing the work of shuttering, along with the petitioner.
He deposed that he used to earn Rs. 25,000/- per month.
He deposed that he has no document to show that he was earning Rs. 25,000/-.

He denied the suggestion that the petitioner was not earning Rs.
25,000/- per month, while working as a labour, for doing the work of shuttering.
He denied the suggestion that he has never worked with the petitioner.
14. Both the respondents failed to lead any evidence during the stage of respondent's evidence.
15. This Tribunal has heard the final arguments as advanced by Sh. Narender Mukhi, Learned counsel for the petitioner and Sh. M. Awasthi, Ld.
Counsel
for insurance co/R2
. None has appeared on behalf of R1 for addressing arguments.

16. On appreciation of evidence as adduced by the petitioner in support of his version, the issue-wise findings of this Tribunal are reproduced herein below:
1.Whether on 11.02.2018, at about 7:45 p.m., at Rishi Nagar, Road no. 43, Opposite Shakur Basti Railway Station, Delhi, one car bearing registration no. DL-3SBN-1849,
which was being driving rashly and negligently by Gopal Kishan, hit the motorcycle bearing registration no. DL8CW-6912 and caused injuries to Shyam Singh?

OPP. 
17.
In the present matter, when issues were framed, in issue no. 1 inadvertently, the vehicles number were wrongly mentioned, as the victim's vehicle which was a motorcycle was bearing registration no.

Sham Singh vs Gopal Kishan on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148486341/
6 DL-3SBN-1849 and the offending car was bearing No. DL-8CW-6912 but inadvertently, against the car, the registration number of motorcycle was mentioned and against the motorcycle, the registration number of offending car was mentioned in issue no. 1.
Therefore, the same being a typographical mistake stands corrected, as no prejudice would be caused to either of the party, as a result of the said correction.
18. The onus of proving this issue on preponderance of probabilities was upon the petitioner/claimant.
19. To prove the aspect of rashness and negligence of R1, in driving the offending vehicle, the petitioner/injured Shyam Singh got himself examined as PW1.

In his evidence affidavit Ex. PW1/A,
PW1 deposed that on 11.02.2018, at about 7:45 p.m., when he along with his son in law namely Baljeet Singh, were going towards Shakur Basti Railway Station and reached near Haryana Maitri Bhawan, at road no. 44, Rani Bagh, Delhi, on their Hero Honda motorcycle bearing registration No.
DL-3SBN- 1849, on which, injured Baljeet Singh was sitting as a pillion rider, they were hit from behind, by one Ritz Car bearing registration no. DL-8CW-6912, which was being driven at a very high speed, rashly, negligently, dangerously, in a zig-zag manner and without blowing horn, by its driver Gopal Kishan/R1, due to which, they both fell down on the metallic road.
PW1 further deposed that he has sustained grievous injuries on spine, which was later diagnosed fracture and his son in law namely Baljeet Singh suffered simple injuries.
He further deposed that the PCR van took them to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, where they received medical treatment.

20 . During the course of cross examination of PW1, though suggestions were put to PW1, by Ld.
Counsel for R2, that the accident has taken place due to negligent driving of the victim's vehicle by PW1, that at the time of accident, neither PW1 nor Baljeet Singh were wearing helmets and that PW1 was driving the victim's vehicle in a drunk state but, PW1 denied the said suggestions.

Further,
suggestions were put to PW1, that on the relevant day, the victim's vehicle was un-insured and that PW1 was driving his vehicle, without holding valid driving license and PW1 admitted both the suggestions.

By putting the said suggestions, Ld. Counsel for R2/insurance company, was trying the prove that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of victim's vehicle by PW1 and by not possessing driving license, PW1 was also guilty of contributory negligence but, R2 failed to elicit any admission from the testimony of PW1 in this regard.

Merely because, PW1 was driving his vehicle, without holding valid driving license, as admitted by PW1, during the course of his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for R2, the same is no ground for giving any finding to the effect that PW1 was also negligent or has contributed to the accident in question, in view of the observations of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Ors, Appeal (Civil) no. 3321 of 2008.

entities.text: Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Ors, Appeal (Civil) no. 3321 of 2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, it was observed by Hon'ble Apex Court, that if a person drives a vehicle without license, although he commits an offence however, the same, by itself, may not lead to a finding of negligence, as regards the accident and if he was not driving rashly and negligently, which contributed to the accident, then he would not be held guilty of contributory negligence.

21. In the present matter also, admittedly the petitioner was not holding valid driving license at the time of accident but, insurance company/R2 failed to prove on record as to how, PW1 was rash and negligent, in driving the victim's vehicle, at the time of accident and how the driving of victim's Sham Singh vs Gopal Kishan on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148486341/
7 vehicle by the petitioner/PW1 has contributed to the accident in question.

Accordingly, no finding can be given that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of victim's vehicle by the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on the part of petitioner, in causing the accident in question.
22. Per contra, by his evidence/PW1 has proved that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

It is also noteworthy that R1 failed to contest the claim petition, by filing any written statement therefore, he also deemed to have admitted that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
23.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that driver of the offending vehicle/R1 has ever approached to any higher authority, with respect to his false implication in the present case.

The fact that the injured Shyam Singh has suffered grievous injuries in the case accident, is also duly corroborated by the MLC no. 445/18 dated 11.02.2018 of PW1.
24.

In view of the above said discussion, criminal case record including charge sheet and testimony of PW1 Shyam Singh, it has been proved by preponderance of probabilities, that the case accident had been caused by R1, who was driving the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-8CW-6912, in a rash and negligent manner, at the above said date, time and place and had hit the victim's motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SBN-1849, due to which, the victim Shyam Singh had sustained grievous injuries.
Issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents accordingly.
Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 25.

In view of findings of this Tribunal qua issue No. 1, regarding negligence of R1, resulting in the occurrence of the case accident, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled to compensation in respect of medical expenses, conveyance expenses, special diet charges,
etc., incurred by him.

This Tribunal shall now examine the entire evidence led by the parties,
including the documents of the petitioner for the purpose of arriving at a finding about the quantum of compensation, to which the petitioner is entitled.
Medical Expenses 26.
The petitioner has claimed in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW-1/A, that he had spent a total sum of Rs. 2,00,000/-, on his medical treatment.

However, perusal of the record reveals that in his evidence, the petitioner has placed reliance on 2 medical bills i.e. bill dated 17.03.2018 and bill dated 14.11.2018, as Ex. PW1/2 colly, which is for an aggregate amount of Rs. 970.92/-, for the treatment received by him and expenses incurred by him for purchase of medicines.
27.
During the course of arguments, it was argued by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner, that the petitioner has also placed on record other medical bills.

However, perusal of the record prima facie reveals that on 12 October 2018, though the petitioner has placed on record photocopy of certain Sham Singh vs Gopal Kishan on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148486341/
8 bills but, the petitioner has neither filed original of the same nor proved the said bills, either by his evidence or by summoning any witness.
Further, the IO has also not placed on record any verified bill, along with the DAR.
Thus, the petitioner is not entitled to seek any compensation qua the said bills.

28. And since the petitioner has proved on record medical bills for an aggregate amount of Rs.
970.92/-.Accordingly, the petitioner is awarded Rs. 970.92/-, as compensation under this head.
Special Diet and conveyance 29.
In his evidence, the petitioner/PW1 has deposed that after the accident, he remained on bed rest for six months.
However, the said deposition is not substantiated by any medical document.
There has been further no deposition by PW1 that he has incurred any amount on special/healthy diet or on conveyance, from his residence to hospital and vice versa.

30. But, even in the absence of any such deposition or documentary proof, the requirement of special diet, need to travel to hospital, have to be determined in accordance with the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner.
31. In this context, a perusal of the petitioner's MLC reveals that the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the case accident.

Further, as per the deposition of Dr. Manish Kumar, S.R. Orthopedic,
Dr. BSA Hospital/PW2, who has proved the disability certificate no. 1547, dated 11.05.2018, of the petitioner Ex. PW2/A, due to the accident, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the tune of 12%, in relation to spine, with diagnosis of post traumatic wedge compression, with fracture of D12 vertebral body.

He further deposed that the patient would feel pain while walking on slope,
he cannot climb stairs without support and cannot squat properly.
He further deposed that the patient would feel moderate difficulty in taking turns.

Thus, keeping in view the grievous nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the case accident, with 12% permanent disability in relation to spine, the period of treatment-cum-recuperation, in the case of the petitioner, is ascertained to be about 6 months.

32. Thus, in view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner as well as his period of treatment-cum-recuperation as assessed, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner was required to take some special diet, including nutrition supplements, high protein diet etc., for speedy recovery of the injuries sustained by him in the case accident and was required to incur expenses on travel to various hospitals and clinics from his residence during his treatment period.

Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs. 50,000/-, as compensation to the petitioner under this head, which includes Rs. 25,000/- each towards special diet and conveyance respectively.
Attendant Charges 33.
There has been no deposition of PW1, that he has incurred any amount for hiring any medical attendant, for his care and look after, during his treatment period.

However, taking into Sham Singh vs Gopal Kishan on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148486341/
9 consideration the fact that the petitioner has duly proved that he has sustained grievous injuries,
with permanent disability of 12%, as per disability certificate Ex. PW2/A, therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have felt compelled to avail services of a medical attendant or a family member, as an attendant for self care activities such as, bathing, dressing up, using the rest room, combing his hairs, eating etc., during his treatment cum recuperation period, which is already assessed as 6 months.
Accordingly, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to award Rs. 50,000/-, as compensation to the petitioner under this head.
Compensation due to permanent disability/Loss of future earning capacity due to disability 34.

A perusal of the court records reveals that as per the disability certificate Ex. PW2/A, the petitioner has sustained 12% permanent disability, in relation to his spine, with diagnosis of post traumatic wedge compression with fracture of D12 vertebral body.

Further, as per the evidence of PW2, with the said disability, the petitioner would feel pain while walking on slope, he cannot climb stairs, without support and cannot squat properly and he would feel moderate difficulty in taking turns.
He further deposed that due to the disability, the petitioner would feel considerable difficulty in doing his work of shuttering.

35. It was argued Ld. Counsel for the petitioner, that since the work of shuttering requires physical force as well as lifting of heavy weight therefore, due to the said disability, the petitioner was unable to continue his work, after the accident, which was also proved by his friend/co-worker PW3 therefore, his disability be taken as 100%.
However, apart from the oral deposition of the petitioner/PW1 and his friend/PW3, there is nothing on record, which will prove that after the accident, the petitioner was not able to do any work.

36. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the recent order in case of Rajesh Tyagi & Ors vs Jaibir Singh &
Ors, FAO 842/2003, date of order 09.03.2018 has inter alia held as follows:
"6.4 The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, education and other factors. 6.5. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps:
(i) The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).

Rajesh Tyagi & Ors vs Jaibir Singh &
Ors, FAO 842/2003
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

(iii) The third step is to find out whether :
a) The claimant is totally disabled, earning any kind of livelihood, or Sham Singh vs Gopal Kishan on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148486341/
10 b) Whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or c) Whether he was prevented all restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."

37. In the light of above cited observations made by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, in the decided case of Rajesh Tyagi & Ors vs Jaibir Singh & Ors (supra), it can be safely concluded that same percentage of permanent disability can have different impact on functional capacity and earning potential of an individual depending upon the nature of his job.

entities.text: Rajesh Tyagi & Ors vs Jaibir Singh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the functional disability has to be ascertained, taking into consideration its impact on the work of the claimant.
38. In the present matter, the petitioner/PW1 deposed that prior to the accident, he was doing the work of shuttering (saria baandhne ka kaam) and his monthly income was Rs. 25,000/-.

Further, as per the deposition of PW2, due to the disability, the petitioner can do the work of shuttering but,
with considerable difficulty therefore, his efficiency in discharging his work of shuttering must have reduced but, not completely restricted.

Therefore, his functional disability cannot be taken as 100%,
as deposed by PW1 or as argued by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner.
